side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: Against Chaos, Gozuki and graveyard-based Fusion decks, it applies pressure and stops the opponent from banishing cards from either graveyard. It does not stop Miracle Fusion or Dragon's Mirror from using only materials on the field. Two copies compensate for the lack of a searcher; the plans replace supporting cards while keeping at least nine Amazoness monsters.

side_cards.name: Cipher Soldier
side_cards.reason: Against Warrior and Amazoness decks, it wins battles without filling the deck with removal that feeds Village. As an EARTH Machine with 1350 ATK, it can be summoned by Giant Rat, but not searched by Wasteland or ROTA.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: An anti-burn monster that preserves the battle plan and Village. Its 1600 ATK means Giant Rat CANNOT summon it, even though it is an EARTH Beast. Two copies compensate for the lack of a searcher.

side_cards.name: Seven Tools of the Bandit
side_cards.reason: Protects important attacks and summons without negating Archers or your own defensive and revival traps. Two copies against traps; each costs 1000 LP and cannot answer the effects of traps that are already active.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Removes Decree, Skill Drain, Oppression and backrow without touching Village. Two copies handle persistent locks that Seven Tools cannot remove once they have resolved.

side_cards.name: Spell Shattering Arrow
side_cards.reason: Destroys opposing Field Spells, Future Fusion and Continuous Spells while preserving your own Village. Bring both copies only against decks with enough face-up Spell targets, not against backrow made entirely of traps.

side_cards.name: D.D. Warrior
side_cards.reason: A battle-based answer to a large or recurring boss monster. An EARTH Warrior with 1200 ATK, accessible through ROTA, Rat and Wasteland. This is a single toolbox option, distinct from the LIGHT D.D. Warrior Lady.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: One answer to set defenders and FLIP monsters that requires no battle and does not trigger battle recruiters. It preserves the Amazoness core without adding another Normal Summon.

side_cards.name: Bottomless Trap Hole
side_cards.reason: A second copy overall against large Warriors and monsters best dealt with by banishing. One extra copy avoids overloading on traps; it is not an answer to every monster summoned during the Damage Step.

side_plans.note: 4 in, 4 out. Keep nine Amazoness monsters, all three Village and every recruiter. Rat can summon Cipher; ROTA, Rat and Wasteland can access D.D. Warrior. None of those cards makes Cipher a Warrior. Remove Tribe because declaring Warrior would also destroy your own board.

3 in, 3 out. Keep nine Amazoness monsters and every searcher. Kycoo stops the opponent from banishing from graveyards, not from the field or hand. D.D. Warrior removes a boss through battle, but also banishes itself and cannot trigger Village because it is not an Amazoness.

side_plans.matchup: Field Spells, Future Fusion and Continuous Spell engines
side_plans.note: 4 in, 4 out. Arrow preserves Village while disrupting the opposing engine; Dust handles traps that Arrow cannot touch. Keep Enemy Controller and both Book of Moon as monster interaction.

side_plans.matchup: Burn / stall with Continuous Spells and Traps
side_plans.note: 8 in, 8 out, only after confirming a lock involving both Spells and Traps. Keep the entire Amazoness lineup, Village and its recruiters. Rat cannot summon Wombat; removing Ring and dead defensive cards reduces LP risk. Do not bring in Arrow without enough observed face-up targets.
3 in, 3 out. A small change to protect your pressure and remove a set wall. Keep ten Amazoness monsters; Tools protects a key attack without shutting off Archers or Call.

side_cards.name: Falling Down
side_cards.reason: While you control a face-up Archfiend, equip this to the best opposing monster and take control of it for as long as it remains equipped. During each opposing Standby Phase, it deals 800 damage to you. This is damage, not a cost, and Pandemonium does not prevent it.

side_cards.name: Deck Devastation Virus
side_cards.reason: General, Terrorking, Mist and Skull can pay its cost. It heavily punishes engines built around recruiters, Flip monsters and low-ATK walls.

side_cards.name: Gemini Imps
side_cards.reason: Protects your hand against Thestalos, Spirit Reaper, Don Zaloog, Card Destruction and Morphing Jar, replaces itself with a draw, and is still a DARK Fiend.

side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: Applies pressure with 1800 ATK and, while on the field, prevents the opponent from banishing cards from graveyards for Chaos, Miracle Fusion or Dragon's Mirror. Those two Fusion Spells can still use materials exclusively from the field.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Chainable removal for Field Spells, Future Fusion and floodgates without shutting off your many traps. It also lets you set another Trap.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Negates the Normal Summon-triggered effects of Monarchs, Gadgets and Breaker, and destroys them.

side_cards.name: Mask of Restrict
side_cards.reason: Shuts down Tribute Summons of Monarchs and other bosses. The corresponding plan removes Skull Archfiend so it does not become a stranded card in your own hand.

side_cards.name: Royal Oppression
side_cards.reason: A transformation against Fusion, Dragon and Zombie decks. The plan removes Roar, Premature, Call and Desrook so your intended Special Summon lines are not left exposed to the opponent using Oppression.

side_plans.note: Mask shuts down the Tribute Summon line, Rug answers the summon-triggered effect, and Gemini Imps prevents Thestalos from turning the exchange into advantage.

side_plans.matchup: HERO Fusion / Red-Eyes / Dragon Future / Zombie
side_plans.note: Remove all four revival cards and Desrook, whose resolution outside the Damage Step could be negated by paying 800 LP. Kycoo blocks materials the opponent wants to banish from their graveyard, while Dust answers Future Fusion, Call of the Mummy and Continuous cards.
Kycoo prevents the opponent from banishing LIGHT and DARK monsters from their graveyard, while Dust removes Call, Premature or backrow without interfering with Pandemonium.

Virus destroys Spy in the hand or face-down, along with low-ATK engines, but a face-up Spy under Necrovalley has 1700 ATK and survives. After its initial resolution, it checks each draw until the end of the opponent's third turn; it does not continually inspect cards added by searches. Falling Down takes a face-up defender or boss while you keep an Archfiend on the field.
Falling Down takes the monster instead of merely destroying it, while Dust removes Village, Hunting Ground and set protection.

side_cards.name: Soul Release
side_cards.reason: Removes fuel for opposing Chaos, Gozuki and Dragon's Mirror without using your Normal Summon or shutting down your own graveyard for Keel and Future.

side_cards.name: Royal Command
side_cards.reason: Against Spy, Guard, Dekoichi, Crystal Seer and other FLIP monsters. This Main Deck has no FLIP monsters of its own, so it provides persistent negation while Armed develops instead of adding another generic Crossout.

side_cards.name: Stamping Destruction
side_cards.reason: Brings the total to three with the Main Deck copy. Remove Necrovalley, Oppression, Drain or traps before leveling up. It requires your own Dragon; Keel is a Machine and is not enough by itself.

side_cards.name: Giant Trunade
side_cards.reason: Creates an attack or level-up window against several Continuous cards. It gains tempo rather than destroying cards, and also returns your own Future Fusion and Equip cards.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Trades one card for a Monarch or Gadget's Normal Summon-triggered effect without requiring a discard. It does not cover Special Summon-triggered effects or Chaos.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Against burn and Solar Flare, a 1600 ATK threat that prevents effect damage, not battle damage or LP costs.

side_cards.name: Divine Wrath
side_cards.reason: Negates Chaos's banishing effect or Fusion Monster effects that My Body cannot cover. Sinister or Dragons you want in the graveyard can pay the discard, but this negation is never free.

side_cards.name: My Body as a Shield
side_cards.reason: Preserves an evolved Armed Dragon against mass or single-target destruction. This Quick-Play Spell does not negate your traps, but it does not protect against banishing, returning to the hand or summon negation.

side_plans.matchup: Chaos Control / Chaos Warrior with an active graveyard
side_plans.note: Keep one Future Fusion, all three Flying Kamakiri #1 and every LV monster; remove this list's only Level Up! Soul Release is preventive, while Divine Wrath answers Chaos's effect, not its summon.

side_plans.matchup: Gravekeeper / control with many FLIP monsters
side_plans.note: Royal Command does not affect any of your own Main Deck monsters. Prioritize removing Necrovalley. Stamping Destruction requires a face-up Dragon; Cyberdark Keel alone is not enough.
Use Rug against Normal Summon-triggered effects. My Body only answers effects that destroy monsters, so it does not cover Thestalos or Mobius. Keep the recruiter core and all three LV5.

Remove the less useful summon responses and part of the delayed engine. Keep Mirror Force, Torrential Tribute, Ring of Destruction and Call of the Haunted; the cards brought in protect your development without negating those traps.

side_plans.matchup: Burn / Pyro focused on Solar Flare
side_plans.note: Wombat does not make costs free. Against battle-focused Pyro, keep Mirror Force and remove a Future Fusion instead. The written plan assumes effect damage or a lock is the main threat.

side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: Brings the total to three with the Main Deck copy: DARK pressure and a block on opposing graveyard banishing against Chaos, Gozuki and graveyard-based Fusions, without stopping your own Chaos. Miracle Fusion and Dragon's Mirror can still use only materials on the field. The two additional copies replace slow DARK monsters, not LIGHTs.

side_cards.name: Soul Release
side_cards.reason: Proactively removes up to five cards before Sorcerer, Book of Life or Miracle Fusion can use them. Two copies help you draw it in time. It is not quick interaction: target the opposing graveyard rather than removing your own materials.

side_cards.name: Cipher Soldier
side_cards.reason: A battle answer to Blade Knight, Don and Amazoness without spending the Chaos engine. Two copies improve the chance of drawing it naturally; it is neither LIGHT nor searchable with ROTA.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: A reactive answer to Decree, Necrovalley and Continuous Traps that keeps your nine traps active. Two copies reinforce Heavy and MST without requiring another Normal Summon.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Negates the Normal Summon-triggered effects of Gadgets and Monarchs, and destroys them. Two copies check their early advantage; it does not cover Special Summons or graveyard effects.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Two monsters against effect damage let you attack while clearing the lock; they do not prevent battle damage. Remove redundant battle defense, not LIGHT monsters.

side_cards.name: Mirage Dragon
side_cards.reason: An additional LIGHT that blocks opposing trap activations during the Battle Phase, such as Mirror Force and Sakuretsu, without negating your own traps. One copy avoids crowding your Normal Summons. It does not negate active traps or protect its own summon.

side_cards.name: Divine Wrath
side_cards.reason: Answers monster effects that later removal cannot solve, including graveyard effects. Only one copy, since the deck already has Tribe and two Raigeki Break. Prefer discarding Serpent or a redundant Thunder; discard Night Assailant only if another FLIP monster can be recovered from the graveyard.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: A second copy overall for set defenders and FLIP engines. One is enough alongside the two existing Book of Moon. Avoid using it automatically in a Spy mirror, since it can also banish your own Spies from the Deck.

side_plans.note: 5 in, 5 out. Keep all six LIGHT monsters and both Sorcerers; Kycoo replaces slow DARKs. Soul Release is preventive, while Wrath supplies the interruption. Do not also remove Thunder Dragons or add Banisher.

3 in, 3 out. Cipher wins battles; Wrath answers monster effects, not Village's Spell effect. Do not give the opponent graveyard or hand resources with Card Destruction. Keep all six LIGHT monsters, your removal and both Spies.

3 in, 3 out. Rug prevents the effect's advantage instead of merely destroying the monster afterward. Wrath broadens your coverage. Keep Brain Control to turn the opponent's Tribute Summon into pressure.

5 in, 5 out. Wombat protects your LP, Dust breaks the lock, and Mirage protects only the Battle Phase. Heavy, MST and Raigeki Break remain for traps that are already active. Adding Mirage brings the LIGHT total to seven.

side_plans.matchup: Wall Rock / set defenders and backrow
side_plans.note: 4 in, 4 out. Use Crossout on set defenders, Dust on Weapon Change, Canyon and locks, and Mirage to prevent new battle trap activations. Do not apply this automatically in a Spy mirror; check which FLIP monster Crossout will banish from both Decks.

side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: Brings the total to three to win the graveyard race while preserving DARK count. It applies 1800 ATK pressure without stopping your own Sorcerer; two copies replace less useful threats in this matchup. It only prevents the opponent from banishing from graveyards, so Miracle Fusion and Dragon's Mirror can still use materials exclusively on the field.

side_cards.name: Soul Release
side_cards.reason: Removes Chaos materials and revival targets before they are used. Two copies reinforce the Kycoo plan without subjecting your own graveyard to continuous banishing.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Removes locks, Decree and Field Spells without shutting down Bottomless, Sakuretsu, Mirror Force or Call. Quick responses are preferred over another Tribute monster competing for the Normal Summon.

side_cards.name: Seven Tools of the Bandit
side_cards.reason: Protects a key summon or attack from Counter Traps and battle traps, and can also negate Decree's activation. Two copies support your pressure without disabling your eight traps. Each use costs 1000 LP.

side_cards.name: Cipher Soldier
side_cards.reason: Provides favorable battle exchanges against Warriors and Amazoness, even under pressure. It is not a Warrior, so ROTA cannot search it; it does not replace the Blade and Sasuke core.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Stops Gadget and Monarch effects. Two copies rather than three leave room for graveyard and trap answers. Do not bring it in by default against Fusions or recruiters.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Two chances to establish protection from effect damage and attack. Its Type and Attribute do not fuel Chaos, so replace battle Spells and Traps rather than LIGHT monsters.

side_cards.name: Chaos Trap Hole
side_cards.reason: An additional answer to Chaos Sorcerer's inherent Special Summon and the Normal or Flip Summon of LIGHT and DARK monsters. One copy because it costs 2000 LP. It cannot be relied on to negate Ritual or Fusion Summons performed within a Chain.

side_plans.note: 5 in, 5 out. Keep seven LIGHT monsters; the two Kycoos replace the two DARKs removed. Reserve Chaos Trap Hole for Sorcerer or another eligible DARK or LIGHT summon, not a Fusion Summon within a Chain.

4 in, 4 out. Keep every Blade Knight, both Sorcerers, all seven LIGHTs and seven DARKs. Cipher stabilizes battles, while Tools protects your advance. Do not spend Tools and 1000 LP on an irrelevant exchange.
2 in, 2 out. A minimal change that preserves Warrior pressure and monster removal. Rug stops the opponent from gaining advantage from their Normal Summon.
6 in, 6 out. Replace monster removal with LP protection and ways to clear backrow. All seven LIGHTs stay intact. Reserve Tools for a trap that will meaningfully change the turn.

4 in, 4 out. Dust forces a response before you attack; Tools protects the crucial action without invalidating your own traps. Do not negate an irrelevant Counter Trap merely to continue a chain of exchanges.

side_cards.name: Soul Release
side_cards.reason: A graveyard answer that avoids adding non-Dragons that would block Totem. Do not use it before Dimension Fusion if that would let the opponent recover strong banished monsters.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Removes Spy, Guard and FLIP monsters without waiting for your Dragons to win a battle. There are no same-name FLIP monsters of your own to lose.

side_cards.name: Stamping Destruction
side_cards.reason: Up to three copies with the Main Deck card to handle Continuous cards and backrow. Every Main Deck monster is a Dragon.

side_cards.name: Giant Trunade
side_cards.reason: Opens the final Battle Phase and temporarily clears Necrovalley or Oppression without adding Types incompatible with Totem.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Prevents Monarchs and Gadgets from gaining advantage through their Normal Summon-triggered effects while you prepare your own Tribute Summons.

side_cards.name: Royal Decree
side_cards.reason: Only for the anti-trap transformation that removes ALL SIX original traps. Do not add it alongside Call, Bottomless, Compulsory or Rug.

side_cards.name: Mirage Dragon
side_cards.reason: A third Normal Summonable Dragon with 1600 ATK that blocks opposing trap activations during battle. It does not replace Decree against traps outside the Battle Phase or against Continuous Traps that are already active.

side_cards.name: Compulsory Evacuation Device
side_cards.reason: Reactive return-to-hand removal against Chaos, Ritual and Fusion monsters without battling or destroying them. It offsets the slowness of your Tribute monsters and stays out of the Decree plan.

side_cards.name: My Body as a Shield
side_cards.reason: Protects the investment in a Tribute or Fusion monster against destruction. A single supporting copy avoids doubling up on LP costs.

side_plans.matchup: Trap-heavy decks / trap burn: full transformation
side_plans.note: Exactly two traps remain: both Decrees. No card brought in adds a non-Dragon monster. Do not also bring in Rug or Compulsory from other plans. Mirage covers the Battle Phase even without drawing Decree, but it does not stop burn during the Main Phase.
Remove Dimension Fusion so it does not return the opponent's monsters banished by Soul Release. Keep Totem and the remaining Tribute monsters. Compulsory does not belong alongside Decree.
Keep one Dragon's Mirror and one Future Fusion. Rug negates Normal Summon-triggered effects; My Body protects against destruction, not discarding, banishing or returning cards to the hand.
A small change that answers set monsters instead of waiting for a face-up summon with enough ATK.

Reduce the cards that depend on the graveyard. The remaining Totems need Necrovalley removed before reviving themselves. Once on the field, they can still count as two Tributes while the opponent keeps Necrovalley, subject to their effect's requirements.

side_cards.name: Cipher Soldier
side_cards.reason: An EARTH monster with 1350 ATK that any of the three Rats can summon to win battles against Warriors and Amazoness. Two copies support successive exchanges. It is a Machine, so its destruction does not trigger Baboon and it does not receive Battle Ox's piercing effect.

side_cards.name: D.D. Warrior
side_cards.reason: An EARTH Warrior with 1200 ATK, accessible through Rat and ROTA, that banishes a boss through battle. A single toolbox option alongside Exiled, rather than another high-Level monster requiring a Tribute.

side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: Prevents the opponent from banishing cards from graveyards without stopping your own Gigantes or Rock Spirit. It does not block banishing from the field or hand, so Miracle Fusion and Dragon's Mirror can use only field materials. Two copies help you draw it because Rat cannot summon it; remove lower-value monsters for this matchup.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Brings the total to three to break locks before attacking without invalidating your defensive traps or Call. Two additional copies compensate for Earth's lack of themed Spell and Trap removal.

side_cards.name: Pitch-Black Warwolf
side_cards.reason: Protects the Battle Phase from new opposing trap activations without negating your own. As a Beast-Warrior, it works with Battle Ox's piercing effect, but it is DARK with 1600 ATK: Rat cannot summon it and its destruction does not trigger Baboon. Two copies compensate for the lack of a searcher.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Two copies against burn while preserving Momonga. Its 1600 ATK prevents Rat from summoning it. Keeps the attack plan and protects LP, but does not prevent battle damage.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Negates the advantage generated by Gadget and Monarch Normal Summon effects, which cannot be solved simply by increasing ATK. Two copies for this specific matchup.

side_cards.name: Enemy Controller
side_cards.reason: One extra flexible interaction card to change an attacker's position or take a boss and finish the game. It can use a spare recruiter as a Tribute, but Tributing that monster does NOT trigger its battle effect.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: An answer to set defenders that hold up your attacks. Your own Rat and Momonga are not FLIP monsters, so its FLIP clause will not remove all their copies.

side_plans.note: 4 in, 4 out. Keep all three Rats, three Momongas, three Gorillas, two Ox and Baboon. Rat can summon the EARTH toolbox monsters; Controller can use its position-changing mode without costing you a monster. Remove Goblins that become exposed at 0 DEF after attacking.

3 in, 3 out. Keep Rat, Momonga, Baboon and both revival cards; this plan does not use Banisher. D.D. Warrior trades battle for banishing, while Kycoo stops opposing costs that banish from the graveyard.
2 in, 2 out. Trade temporary ATK increases for preventing their summon-triggered advantage. Smashing, Exiled, Brain Control, Book of Moon and the traps remain to deal with monsters that get through.

6 in, 6 out. Keep all three Momongas to stabilize your LP; remove Lily because of its cost. Dust removes active locks. Warwolf only blocks new trap activations during the Battle Phase; it does not protect its own summon or negate an active Continuous Trap.

side_plans.matchup: Wall Rock / Spy and defensive backrow
side_plans.note: 6 in, 6 out. Keep all three Rats and three Momongas. Use Crossout on set defenders, Dust on Weapon Change or Canyon, and Warwolf with Ox for the offensive turn. Controller changes position or takes a monster; do not activate it without a concrete benefit.

side_cards.name: Mobius the Frost Monarch
side_cards.reason: A second legal copy for backrow matchups. It is WATER, preserves material for Frost and Flame Dragon, and turns a small monster into two removals.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Chainable removal for Field Spells, Future Fusion, Call and floodgates without depending on a successful Tribute Summon.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Negates the Normal Summon-triggered effects of Monarchs, Gadgets and Breaker.

side_cards.name: Nightmare Penguin
side_cards.reason: Mother Grizzly can summon it because it has 900 ATK. While face-up, it raises Hydrogeddon from 1600 to 1800 ATK. Being summoned by Grizzly does not trigger its flip effect; it must be set and then flipped face-up to return an opposing card.

side_cards.name: Salvage
side_cards.reason: Recovers exactly two WATER monsters with 1500 ATK or less. The Main Deck offers six targets: two Mother Grizzly, two Crystal Seer, Yomi Ship and Sinister Serpent. Nightmare Penguin adds a seventh. It cannot recover Hydrogeddon at 1600 ATK or Abyss Soldier at 1800.

side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: Pressures the opposing graveyard and prevents the opponent from banishing cards from either graveyard. Its controller can still banish two WATER and one FIRE from their own graveyard to summon the Dragon. It does not prevent banishing from the field.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Stops Solar Flare, Volcanic Slicer, Ring and other effect-damage finishes while providing 1600 ATK.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Removes Spy, Apprentice, Crystal Seer and set walls that stop Hydrogeddon, without triggering their effects.

side_cards.name: Divine Wrath
side_cards.reason: Negates monster effects. The discard can be Sinister Serpent or a monster with an Attribute you wanted to put in the graveyard.

side_plans.note: Three dedicated Spell and Trap answers replace less reliable battle interaction. Mobius still counts as WATER once it reaches the graveyard.
Rug answers the Normal Summon-triggered effect without dismantling the engine. Keep all six Main Deck FIRE monsters, Lonefire and Mobius.

side_plans.matchup: Chaos / Zombie / Dragon's Mirror / Miracle Fusion
side_plans.note: Kycoo blocks the opponent's graveyard banishing without stopping yours. It does not stop materials from being banished from the field. Wrath answers Gozuki, Chaos Sorcerer and other decisive effects.
Wombat stops the effect-damage clock, while Dust removes Molten Destruction or Continuous cards before they build advantage.
Nobleman avoids triggering Flip effects, while Wrath covers the effects that do get to activate.

side_plans.matchup: Chaos Warrior / Earth Aggro / battle control without graveyard hate
side_plans.note: Penguin replaces Mobius as a WATER monster, keeping that Attribute's total unchanged and all six FIRE monsters intact. Bring in Salvage only when you expect to have an accessible graveyard. It recovers two small targets for advantage or Abyss Soldier's discard cost; do not bring it in against Necrovalley or other graveyard hate.

side_cards.name: Royal Oppression
side_cards.reason: Two copies for the anti-Special Summon plan; remove Chief and both Rite of Spirit. There is still a conflict with voluntarily Flip Summoning Spy outside the Damage Step. Establish your monsters before activating Oppression.

side_cards.name: Rivalry of Warlords
side_cards.reason: The entire Main Deck monster lineup is Spellcaster, so two copies punish mixed Types in Chaos and Warrior without requiring an engine transformation. Do not combine this package with Wombat or Mobius, which would prevent you from deploying Spellcasters.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Answers Monarchs and Gadgets before they gain advantage. Two copies are enough alongside the Main Deck Bottomless Traps, leaving room for Field Spell answers.

side_cards.name: Mobius the Frost Monarch
side_cards.reason: One Tribute monster that turns a spare Spy into two backrow removals, especially against locks. A single copy avoids clogging the hand. It cannot coexist with Spellcasters under Rivalry, so they belong in separate plans.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Necrovalley alone is not enough against burn. Two copies help establish protection with an attacker. Spy cannot summon them, and they do not belong in the Rivalry plan.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: A third copy overall for Decree and persistent locks. Only one is needed because the Main Deck already has two, Heavy Storm and MST.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: A second copy for Wall Rock and set defenders without overloading on removal. Not an automatic choice in a Spy mirror: it would also banish your own copies from the Deck.

side_cards.name: Gemini Imps
side_cards.reason: Hand-based protection against Mazera or Thestalos discarding. It replaces itself if it negates and destroys. One copy supports the Rug plan; do not summon it as a Fiend while using Rivalry.

side_cards.name: Spell Shattering Arrow
side_cards.reason: A quick answer to opposing Future Fusion, Field Spells and Continuous Spells that preserves Necrovalley. Two copies let you act before Future resolves. It does not destroy traps or negate Normal Spells.

side_cards.name: Seven Tools of the Bandit
side_cards.reason: Focused protection against Decree's activation or a Counter Trap that would stop you from breaking a lock. One copy because of the LP cost and because Dust already covers active traps.

side_plans.matchup: Fusion / Special Summons and Future Fusion
side_plans.note: 4 in, 4 out. Establish your board before applying the lock; Oppression affects both players. Do not voluntarily Flip Summon Spy expecting the opponent to allow its effect. Battle-triggered recruitment during the Damage Step normally does not offer an Oppression window. Arrow removes Future before it resolves.

2 in, 2 out. Keep every Spellcaster and one Rite of Spirit. Remove Chief so your own graveyard stays sealed. Maintain Necrovalley and do not also bring in Mobius or Wombat. Rivalry does not stop an opposing board whose monsters all share a Type.

3 in, 3 out. Rug answers Gadget and Monarch, while Gemini covers Thestalos and Mazera from the hand. Rug does NOT negate Mazera's Special Summon. Necrovalley does not stop you from sending Gemini from the hand as a cost. Keep Deck Devastation Virus because it is highly valuable against Gadgets.
5 in, 5 out. No Rivalry or Oppression in this plan. Spy provides a Tribute for Mobius, Wombat protects LP, and three Dust Tornado in total handle the lock without negating your own traps.

side_plans.matchup: Wall Rock / defenders and Continuous Spells
side_plans.note: 5 in, 5 out. Crossout removes set defenders, Arrow handles Weapon Change or Canyon, and Mobius clears backrow. Keep Deck Devastation Virus, which is very useful against low-ATK walls, along with Spy, Ambusher and both Rite of Spirit. Leave out Rivalry so the Tribute Summon remains legal. Do not blindly use the same plan against other Spy decks.

side_cards.name: Hero Blast
side_cards.reason: Recovers Sparkman or other Normal HERO monsters for Polymerization and destroys a face-up opposing monster whose ATK is no higher than the recovered monster's. Sparkman sets the ceiling at 1600, so it cannot destroy Chaos or Monarch. Bring it in only when removing both Decrees.

side_cards.name: Elemental HERO Wildheart
side_cards.reason: A second Wildheart, searchable with E-Call or ROTA. It applies trap-immune pressure and is an actual material for Wildedge, Wild Wingman, Necroid Shaman and Gaia.

side_cards.name: De-Fusion
side_cards.reason: Removes opposing Fusions without destroying them and can protect your own Fusion from a targeted effect. Recovering its materials requires all the materials actually used to be in the graveyard, along with enough space. Miracle usually banishes them, and Metamorphosis does not enable this material recovery.

side_cards.name: Soul Release
side_cards.reason: Removes fuel for opposing Chaos, Zombie and Fusion decks while preserving your graveyard for Miracle. As a Spell, it does not conflict with Decree.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Removes Spy, Guard and FLIP monsters that would otherwise force you to spend Fusions. Be careful against Morphing Jar: your Main Deck also uses it, and your copy will be banished if it is still in the Deck.

side_cards.name: Spiritualism
side_cards.reason: An immediate, non-negatable answer to Necrovalley, Oppression, Drain or an attack lock. It opens a Fusion window without waiting for Dust and works under your own Decree. It only returns the card; it does not remove it permanently.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: For effect damage and burn. It is not HERO material, so it stays in the Side Deck until needed. Preserve E-Call, the Normal Monsters and the Fusion routes.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Monarchs and Gadgets gain advantage before Future pays off; Rug stops their Normal Summon trigger. Bringing it in together with Hero Blast requires removing Decree.

side_plans.note: Switch from Decree to interaction: Blast recovers Sparkman and removes Gadgets, while Rug answers Monarch. Do not use Blast as an answer to a 2400 ATK Monarch. Keep one Future Fusion and the entire Poly and Miracle engine.
The only traps left are the two Decrees. Wildheart is searchable and can attack despite opposing traps resolving; Spiritualism clears locks that are already active.
Keep one Miracle for after removing Necrovalley. Do not strip out Poly or E-Call. Decree can negate Oppression, but not Necrovalley; Spiritualism opens that window.

side_plans.matchup: Fusions and graveyards: HERO / Dragon Future / Red-Eyes
side_plans.note: Remove Decree against an opponent with few traps. Using De-Fusion on an opposing Fusion does not return materials from THEIR graveyard: the script requires the activating player's graveyard. Soul Release leaves your own Miracle materials untouched.
Keep both Decrees and every Fusion route. Wombat protects against effect damage, not costs or battle damage. Do not add Hero Blast or Rug while retaining this Decree plan.
A small adjustment: remove their fuel without filling your Main Deck with monsters outside the HERO engine. There is no need to copy the four-card transformation used against Fusion decks.

side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: An 1800 ATK threat that prevents the opponent from banishing from the GYs for Chaos/Gozuki/Miracle; Miracle Fusion and Dragon's Mirror can still use only field materials. Two copies provide access without a searcher. It is neither WIND nor Winged Beast, so it replaces support cards, not the Harpies.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Two copies against effect damage let you keep attacking while HHG clears the way. Kamakiri cannot search it, and it does not protect against battle damage.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Answers Oppression/Decree or Field Spells before Hunting Ground is established. Two copies keep you from relying entirely on summoning a Harpie to remove the Trap that prevents that summon.

side_cards.name: Anti-Spell Fragrance
side_cards.reason: A tempo plan against Spell engines: the opponent's Set Spells become Hunting Ground targets. Two copies help find it early. It also delays your own Egotist, Nest and Book, so establish your plays first.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Stops Gadget/Monarch effects from overwhelming the Harpies. It does not negate Fusions or recruiters; two copies fill that specific role.

side_cards.name: Enemy Controller
side_cards.reason: Changes battle position against combat threats, or takes control of a monster to finish with a wide board. One copy because it overlaps with the two Books; the Tribute is a cost and does not generate value through Hunting Ground.

side_cards.name: Spell Shattering Arrow
side_cards.reason: An additional immediate answer to Future Fusion/Field Spells without returning or destroying your own HHG. One copy because HHG/Queen/Heavy/MST already provide removal; it does not answer Traps.

side_cards.name: Seven Tools of the Bandit
side_cards.reason: Protects your opening development or a decisive attack from Traps without shutting off Party/Icarus/Call. Two copies for backrow matchups; pay 1000 only when it preserves a meaningful play.

side_cards.name: Lightning Vortex
side_cards.reason: The only additional board wipe for a wide face-up board. It can discard a Harpie for Party to revive later, but that remains a real cost, and it does not destroy Set monsters.

side_plans.note: 2 in, 2 out. Keeps all Harpies, Kamakiri, Egotist, Nest and Party. Nine Winged Beasts remain, including eight Level 4 monsters for Nest; Kycoo is not a valid Tribute or search target for those effects.
2 in, 2 out. Keeps Sisters/Oracle/Egotist intact: Rug checks the advantage from opposing Normal Summons while your own engine develops.

3 in, 3 out. Activate HHG and prepare your first wave and Set Spells before Fragrance. All your own Spells are subject to the delay, including Nest. HHG may be forced to destroy one of your own Spells/Traps if no other target is available: do not pile up Field Spells blindly.

7 in, 7 out. Keeps the full Harpie engine and Icarus/Party instead of negating your own Traps. Wombat prevents burn damage, while Arrow/Dust/HHG break the lock; removing Ring avoids dangerous self-damage.

side_plans.matchup: Earth / Amazoness with an established board and battle Traps
side_plans.note: 4 in, 4 out. Keeps both Egotists, both Nests, Sisters, both Oracles and one Party; trades slow revival for immediate interaction. Vortex only hits face-up monsters; Controller can open an attack without Tributing, or take control to finish. Do not treat Tools as an automatic tax on every attack.

side_cards.name: Order to Charge
side_cards.reason: With five actual Normal Monsters and Dai/Birthright, it turns a threatened Normal Monster into non-targeting destruction of an opposing monster. The Tribute happens on resolution, so your Normal Monster must still be valid; it cannot Tribute Pinch Hopper or Tokens.

side_cards.name: Dust Barrier
side_cards.reason: Temporarily protects the five Normal Monsters from the opponent's Smashing/Brain/Soul Exchange/Book without making them immune to your own Spells as Non-Spellcasting Area would. It does not protect Ultimate or other Effect Monsters, and it destroys itself during your second Standby Phase.

side_cards.name: Swarm of Locusts
side_cards.reason: A Howling search target for slow games against Traps and Continuous cards. It destroys on a Flip SUMMON, not when flipped by an attack; it needs to survive and get a genuine opportunity.

side_cards.name: Swarm of Scarabs
side_cards.reason: A second, different Howling target for repeatable advantage against slow monster strategies. Do not bring it in against aggro that will not let you Flip Summon.

side_cards.name: 4-Starred Ladybug of Doom
side_cards.reason: Two FLIP answers to multiple opposing face-up Level 4 monsters, such as Warriors, Amazoness or Gadgets. Howling Insect can summon it face-up, but that does not activate its FLIP effect: normally Set it from hand. It is not a substitute for GY hate and does not destroy monsters of other Levels.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Against Spy/FLIP monsters, clears a path for Insect Knight and Metal Armored Bug. The Swarms are not FLIP monsters and do not activate simply by being flipped face-up.

side_cards.name: Seven Tools of the Bandit
side_cards.reason: Negates the activation of Mirror/Torrential/Bottomless/Oppression without shutting off Birthright and Call. Costs 1000 LP; it does not negate an effect of an Oppression that was already active.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Negates Monarch/Gadget effects on Normal Summon, preserving your large bodies and revival support.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Against Burn/Solar Flare, replaces ineffective LP pressure with continuous protection from effect damage. Neither Howling nor Rat can summon it (1600 ATK).

side_plans.note: Shifts to immediate answers by removing the entire LV line. Keeps all five Normal Monsters, Unexpected Dai, Birthright and Pinch Hopper. Set Ladybug to use its FLIP effect; Order to Charge trades a Normal Monster for an opposing monster. This plan does not banish cards from the GY.

Keeps all five Normal Monsters, one Art, one Pinch and the complete LV line. Dust Barrier protects Normal Monsters from opposing Spells, not Zaborg: Rug answers that trigger. Remove the Main Deck Nobleman if you have not seen relevant FLIP defenders.
Keeps one Metal with one Art, both Pinches and all three Knights. Locust is a Howling toolbox option, not a promise of immediate destruction after being attacked.

Scarabs only needs a Flip Summon and can destroy even defenders you would rather not battle. Against faster control, omit Scarabs from this plan and swap only the two Crossouts. Keep the Main Deck Nobleman for three Crossouts in total. Vortex comes out because it is less precise against Set defenders.

Do not rely on revival under Necrovalley. Locust offers another way to remove the Field Spell alongside Heavy/MST/Breaker/Dust/Gigantes. Seven Tools must answer a Trap's ACTIVATION, not an already active Oppression. Ancient Rules comes out with all four revival cards; keep all three Noblemen for Spy/Guard.

Removes your own LP payments/self-damage and less useful battle responses. Seven Tools costs LP: negate the relevant piece rather than spending it indiscriminately. If the opponent is playing Pyro aggro rather than burn, do not automatically make all five swaps.

side_cards.name: Falling Down
side_cards.reason: With Soldier, General or Mist face-up, equips to and takes control of an opposing monster while it remains equipped, opening Mazera's attack without sacrificing Warrior of Zera. It inflicts 800 damage to you during each opponent's Standby Phase, and Pandemonium does not prevent it.

side_cards.name: Gemini Imps
side_cards.reason: Defends combo pieces against the opponent's discard effects, draws a card and also supplies DARK/Fiend fuel for Dark Necrofear when used.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: A tempo answer to Monarchs, Gadgets and Breaker without committing Warrior of Zera.

side_cards.name: Bottomless Trap Hole
side_cards.reason: Banishes Monarchs and Fusion/Chaos bosses. The Main Deck has no copies, so two can come in without exceeding the limit.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Removes Necrovalley, Village, Hunting Ground, Royal Oppression and backrow before the combo turn.

side_cards.name: Spiritualism
side_cards.reason: Its activation and effect cannot be negated; temporarily removes a face-up floodgate or backrow card during the decisive turn.

side_cards.name: Soul Release
side_cards.reason: Removes Chaos, Zombie and GY Fusion materials at once by targeting only the opponent's GY.

side_cards.name: My Body as a Shield
side_cards.reason: Protects Warrior of Zera or Mazera from Torrential, Bottomless, Vortex and monster destruction during the critical window.

side_plans.note: Rug and Bottomless cover the summon; Gemini Imps stops Thestalos from breaking up your combo hand, and removing Card Destruction avoids refilling the Gadget player's hand.

Soul Release removes materials only from the opponent's GY, while Dust cuts off Continuous cards and revival. Necrofear comes out because it is slow and requires its own setup, not because Soul Release affects your GY.
Three Spell/Trap answers clear Necrovalley or Oppression, while My Body protects Zera/Mazera from the destructive response.
Keep Soldier/General to support Falling Down; Bottomless handles large bodies, and My Body protects your push.
Gemini Imps comes in only when you have seen discard caused by an opponent's effect; it is not meant to answer discards paid as costs.

side_cards.name: Banisher of the Radiance
side_cards.reason: A consistent anti-GY transformation: Gigantes and Rock Spirit come out. This Main Deck has no revival cards; all nine Gadgets still search on the field. Two anti-GY bodies, not three that would overcrowd your Normal Summons.

side_cards.name: The End of Anubis
side_cards.reason: A 2500 ATK Tribute monster that negates effects activated in the GY or targeting it, including Gozuki's GY effect and targeted revival; it does not stop Gozuki from sending cards from the Deck. Replaces a Monarch rather than adding another Tribute monster. It does not negate Miracle/Dragon's Mirror, which banish without targeting.

side_cards.name: Mind Crush
side_cards.reason: Disrupts cards known from public Gadget, Manju or E - Emergency Call searches. Both you and your opponent must have at least one card in hand to activate it. Two copies attack hand redundancy without discarding from your own hand unless you miss; do not name cards blindly or discard Despair from the Dark.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: A direct answer in the Gadget/Monarch mirror. Two copies leave room for other matchups and do not require the monster to remain vulnerable to battle destruction.

side_cards.name: Cipher Soldier
side_cards.reason: Against Warriors/Amazoness, provides a low-Level body that both attacks and defends to support Tributes. Gadgets do not search it, and the deck does not have Rat.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Two anti-burn bodies that can still apply pressure; trim less useful Tribute monsters and removal to avoid losing to a clogged hand.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: The third copy overall, to cut off an opponent's response or remove an active Continuous card. One copy here because the deck already has two Mobius, Heavy and MST.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: An answer to Set defenders/FLIP monsters that avoids giving away battle advantage. One copy alongside the Main Deck's three Smashings, since they cover different battle positions.

side_cards.name: Seven Tools of the Bandit
side_cards.reason: Protects the investment in a Tribute Summon from Solemn/other Traps and enables a decisive attack. Two copies without shutting off your own eight-Trap package; each use costs 1000 LP.

side_plans.note: 3 in, 3 out. Removes both of your own banishing costs so you do not depend on a GY that Banisher empties. Keeps nine Gadgets and seven Tribute monsters by replacing Thestalos with Anubis. Anubis is not a universal negator of Fusions that banish materials.
3 in, 3 out. Drops from seven to five Tribute monsters for faster defense while keeping nine Gadgets. Crossout removes only Set monsters; Cipher holds the board for your remaining Tribute monsters.

4 in, 4 out. Rug stops the Normal Summon from generating value. Use Mind Crush after seeing the card added by Gadget and before it leaves the opponent's hand, keeping at least one card in your own hand so you can activate it. Keeps all nine Gadgets and seven Monarchs.

5 in, 5 out. Keeps both Mobius for backrow, drops to five Tribute monsters and avoids dead control-taking/Tribute Spells. Wombat establishes protection, while Dust removes Continuous cards; spend LP on Tools only to establish or preserve that protection.

5 in, 5 out. Mind Crush requires a card in your own hand and information from E - Emergency Call, Manju or a Polymerization search, not a guess. Tools protects Tribute monsters from Trap activations, not effects of already face-up Traps; Dust retains an answer to Future/Continuous cards. Six Tribute monsters, nine Gadgets and monster removal remain. Do not use this discard against Despair when it would benefit from being sent by the opponent.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Wins the burn mirror by reducing damage from Solar Flare, Volcanic Slicer and Traps to zero while still providing 1600 ATK.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Chainable removal for Field Spells, Future Fusion, Call and floodgates while keeping your own Traps active.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: A clean trade against Monarchs, Gadgets and Breaker.

side_cards.name: Mask of Restrict
side_cards.reason: Shuts down opposing Tribute Summons; the plan removes both of your own Thestalos copies.

side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: Prevents the opponent from banishing cards from the GYs for Chaos or Fusions without stopping its controller from banishing FIRE monsters from their own GY for Spirit of Flames. Does not stop materials from being banished from the field.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Clears a path for Pyro attackers through Spy, Apprentice and walls without triggering their FLIP effects.

side_cards.name: Divine Wrath
side_cards.reason: Negates monster effects. Discarding a FIRE monster is not a total loss because Oil can recover two different names.

side_cards.name: Ceasefire
side_cards.reason: The deck has no FLIP effects of its own. On resolution, it flips Set monsters without activating their FLIP effects during that resolution and adds a burn finisher that fits the Pyro plan.

side_plans.note: Thestalos and Gaia Soul come out; Gaia Soul's optional ATK boost also Tributes Pyro monsters. Rug covers both Monarch effects and the Gadget chain.
Kycoo prevents the opponent from banishing from the GYs, while Wrath answers monster engines; discarded FIRE monsters remain recoverable with Oil.

side_plans.matchup: Gravekeeper / Harpie / Amazoness / Field Spell backrow
side_plans.note: Dust handles Spell/Trap removal without spending a discard, letting you reserve Oil for rebuilding your monsters.
Nobleman removes two specific threats, while Ceasefire reveals the rest without activating their FLIP effects during that resolution and brings you closer to lethal damage.
Wombat makes effect damage harmless, while Dust removes the Field Spell or Continuous cards driving the opponent's damage clock.

side_cards.name: Stamping Destruction
side_cards.reason: A Dragon is frequently on the field, making this a Spell-based answer to Necrovalley/Oppression/Drain without disabling Red-Eyes Spirit. Paladin is a Dragon; Manju is not.

side_cards.name: Giant Trunade
side_cards.reason: Opens a window for Ritual Summons, revival or attacks against backrow. It also returns your own Continuous and Equip cards: activate it before investing in Future or after getting value from it, not as a free board clear.

side_cards.name: Soul Release
side_cards.reason: Removes the opponent's GY without blocking your own Wyvern/Spirit/Mirror. Banisher is not added to solve one matchup at the cost of creating another internal conflict.

side_cards.name: Compulsory Evacuation Device
side_cards.reason: An answer to Chaos, Ritual and Fusion monsters that does not rely on winning battles or destroying them. Do not use it indiscriminately against Manju/Gadgets that would search again.

side_cards.name: Mind Crush
side_cards.reason: Against search engines, remove the piece after seeing what Manju/Ragged/E-Call/Gadget searched. You need a card in your own hand and should not guess blindly; discarding an opposing Red-Eyes can help the opponent if you choose the wrong piece.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Protection against burn while the Future/Ritual route develops. It does not depend on the GY or Traps, and creates no Totem conflict because this Main Deck does not use Totem.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Against Monarchs/Gadgets/Manju, negates the effect on Normal Summon and destroys its source. An alternative to Mind Crush's discard depending on your hand and the turn.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Removes Spy/Guard and other FLIP monsters blocking Red-Eyes. Complements Paladin without first requiring a Ritual Summon and an attack.

side_plans.note: Removes five GY-dependent cards while keeping the Ritual routes from hand/Deck. The remaining Wyvern and Mirror need Necrovalley removed to be useful.

One Future, one Dark Dragon Ritual, ARA, Ragged and three Manjus remain: the engine stays intact with a lower ceiling and fewer slow-tempo cards. Compulsory can remove Chaos in response to its effect, but does not negate it; an already activated effect still resolves if its target remains valid.

Use Mind Crush on the Gadget actually added to the hand or otherwise known; do not assume you know a hidden Monarch. Rug negates the Normal Summon trigger. Do not spend both cards on the same search that Rug already negated.
Keeps both Spirits and Call, which is why Decree is not added. Stamping requires a face-up Dragon and can use Paladin/Luster/Masked/Red-Eyes.
Keeps the Ritual engine and Red-Eyes recursion. Wombat buys the time Future needs; the Spells remove attack barriers and continuous damage sources.

side_plans.matchup: HERO / Ritual / Red-Eyes with revealed searches
side_plans.note: Trades battle-based removal for interaction with engine pieces and the GY. Use Mind Crush on a searched Ritual/Fusion Spell; avoid discarding fuel that gives the opponent an advantage. Compulsory returns Fusion Monsters to the Extra Deck.

side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: DARK pressure against Chaos/Zombie without banishing your own pieces. Your Kycoo prevents the OPPONENT from banishing from the GYs, not your own Chaos summons.

side_cards.name: Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell
side_cards.reason: Against a repeated engine Spell (Future/Miracle/Ritual) or a Field Spell that has not resolved yet, a redundant Spell pays to negate, destroy and lock out the opponent's future copies. Do not use it if you must discard your only Ritual route.

side_cards.name: Seven Tools of the Bandit
side_cards.reason: Protects Ritual Summons and absorption against Trap activations without disabling Raigeki Break or Call. Costs 1000 LP and does not answer the effect of an already active Continuous Trap.

side_cards.name: Compulsory Evacuation Device
side_cards.reason: Against Fusion/Ritual/Chaos monsters or a monster you cannot absorb. A non-destruction answer; returning your own Relinquished requires another Ritual Summon, so it is not a free reset.

side_cards.name: Divine Wrath
side_cards.reason: Negates Chaos/Monarch/Harpie effects and protects Relinquished from removal by monster effects. Sinister can pay the cost, but the card still requires a discard.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Against burn while Relinquished limits attacks. Both Chaos copies come out in this plan so you do not need to support another engine alongside Ritual.

side_cards.name: Giant Trunade
side_cards.reason: Temporarily removes Necrovalley/Oppression/Drain and opens absorption/Ritual plays. It also returns cards equipped to Relinquished to their owners' hands; evaluate that before activating it.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Removes Spy/Guard/FLIP monsters without absorbing a low-ATK monster. Against an opposing Old Vindictive, it can banish yours from the Deck; keeping Tsukuyomi and Apprentice does not remove that caveat.

side_plans.note: Removes the entire three-Spellcaster slow recruiter package. Keeps all six LIGHT monsters and five Ritual searchers. Kycoo only removes GY cards when it deals damage, and its banishing restriction applies only to the opponent.

Removes the slow Flip package, not part of the Ritual engine. Cursed Seal requires a Spell discard and successful destruction to apply its lasting lock. Compulsory returns Fusion Monsters to the Extra Deck; it does not negate already activated effects.

Wrath negates the effect when it activates; Compulsory does not, so save it for another threat or to remove an attacker. Avoid routinely returning Gadgets. Do not combine this plan with another that removes the same three monsters.

Keeps Raigeki Break for interaction and keeps Call. Seven Tools answers activations; use Heavy/MST/Breaker/Trunade for an already active Continuous card. Trunade can return the monster equipped to Relinquished to the opponent's hand.

Three Relinquished, two Black Illusions, one ARA, two Raggeds and all searchers remain. Abandons Chaos under Necrovalley; Relinquished does not depend on the GY to absorb monsters. Seven Tools removes neither Necrovalley nor an already face-up Oppression.
A pure Ritual plan: Wombat covers effect damage, and Relinquished applies pressure without taking Ring's self-damaging trade. Save the LP payment for Seven Tools for an important piece.

side_cards.name: Dark Renewal
side_cards.reason: Uses any face-up Spellcaster to remove an opposing summon and converts the trade into Dark Magician of Chaos or another DARK Spellcaster from the Deck/GY.

side_cards.name: Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
side_cards.reason: Completes the three legal copies alongside the Main Deck copy. A DARK Spellcaster with 1800 ATK that prevents the opponent from banishing cards from the GYs for Chaos, Miracle Fusion or Dragon's Mirror. Those two Fusion Spells can still use field materials.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Removes Field Spells and floodgates without Raigeki Break's discard and lets you Set a control Trap.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Negates Monarch, Gadget and Breaker effects in their Normal Summon window.

side_cards.name: Mind Crush
side_cards.reason: Punishes confirmed information from Gadget, Commandant, Harpie Queen, E - Emergency Call and Reinforcement of the Army.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Alongside the Main Deck copy, reaches three against Spy, Apprentice and Wall without exposing a Spellcaster to combat.

side_cards.name: Divine Wrath
side_cards.reason: A universal answer to monster effects; discarding LIGHT/DARK monsters prepares Chaos Sorcerer and revival plays.

side_cards.name: Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell
side_cards.reason: The high Spell count supports its cost and prevents further activations of the same name for the rest of the Duel, such as Future Fusion, Miracle Fusion, Book of Life or Dark Spirit's Mastery. The restriction does not carry over to other Duels in the Match.

side_plans.note: Rug negates the effect activated on Normal Summon, Mind Crush uses the card revealed by Gadget, and Wrath covers effects outside that window. Keeps all six Main Deck LIGHT monsters to support both copies of Chaos Sorcerer.

side_plans.matchup: Amazoness / Earth Aggro / Armed Dragon / Insect
side_plans.note: Renewal turns a small Spellcaster into removal plus a DARK Spellcaster, while Wrath prevents the monster engine from regaining tempo. None of the six LIGHT monsters for Chaos Sorcerer are cut.

side_plans.matchup: Chaos / Zombie / HERO / Dragon Future / Red-Eyes
side_plans.note: Kycoo prevents the opponent from banishing materials from the GYs without stopping your own Chaos plays; it does not block field materials. Save Cursed Seal for the repeated Spell that defines the opponent's engine during that Duel.
Dust avoids paying a discard to remove Field Spells, while Cursed Seal punishes the repeated Spell once you have identified it.
Three Noblemen including the Main Deck copy reduce the need to attack Spy, Apprentice, Crystal Seer or Set walls while keeping all six Main Deck LIGHT monsters for Chaos Sorcerer.

side_cards.name: Limiter Removal
side_cards.reason: All three Gear Golems are Machines. After Weapon Change, it doubles 2200 ATK to 4400 and turns the defensive plan into a real finish, including through a direct attack. It destroys the Machines in the End Phase, so save it as a finisher.

side_cards.name: Shield Crush
side_cards.reason: Destroys Defense Position monsters without flipping them, answering Spy, Apprentice and the wall mirror without activating their effects.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Chainable removal against Field Spells, Continuous cards and backrow while preserving your own Trap engine.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Negates Monarch and Gadget effects before they turn the slow game into advantage.

side_cards.name: Mask of Restrict
side_cards.reason: Prevents opposing Tribute Summons; Guardian Sphinx comes out in this plan so it does not get stuck in your hand.

side_cards.name: My Body as a Shield
side_cards.reason: Protects your accumulated board from Smashing, Lightning Vortex, Torrential and other mass or targeted destruction.

side_cards.name: Disappear
side_cards.reason: Chained to Call, Premature or Book of Life, removes the GY target and makes the relevant revival fail.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Covers a defensive strategy's natural weakness to Solar Flare, Volcanic Slicer, Ring and other damage sources that do not need to attack.

side_plans.note: Guardian Sphinx comes out because Mask of Restrict would prevent its Tribute Summon. Pulling the Rug answers Gadget and Monarch effects activated on Normal Summon.
Disappear removes the GY target in the Chain, while Dust removes Call of the Mummy, Premature, Call or Future Fusion.
Shield Crush removes defenders without flipping them; Limiter Removal gives Gear Golem a damage route once the game is stabilized.
My Body protects the walls from destruction, while Dust forces the opponent to respond before accumulating backrow.
Wombat stops damage that bypasses combat, while Dust removes Molten Destruction or Continuous cards before the finish.

side_cards.name: Tutan Mask
side_cards.reason: A dedicated Counter Trap that protects a face-up Zombie from Book of Moon, Ring, Enemy Controller, Compulsory and other single-target Spells/Traps.

side_cards.name: Deck Devastation Virus
side_cards.reason: Ryu Kokki, Vampire Lord and Despair can pay the cost. Destroys monsters with 1500 ATK or less seen on the field/in hand and on each draw until the end of the opponent's third turn after activation.

side_cards.name: Disappear
side_cards.reason: Chained to Call, Premature or Book of Life, banishes the key target from the opponent's GY without shutting down your own GY.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Negates Monarch, Gadget and Breaker Normal Summon effects when they resolve.

side_cards.name: Mask of Restrict
side_cards.reason: Shuts down opposing Tribute Summons while your large Zombies retain Book of Life, Call of the Mummy, Gozuki, Premature and Call as Special Summon routes.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Removes Necrovalley, Royal Oppression and backrow that would block revival without negating your own Traps.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Removes Spy, Apprentice and walls without allowing their FLIP effects, opening attacks for Ryu Kokki or Vampire Lord.

side_cards.name: Divine Wrath
side_cards.reason: Negates monster effects, and discarding a Zombie helps Book of Life, Call, Premature or Gozuki's second effect.

side_plans.note: Zombie bosses still enter through Special Summons; Rug covers the summon that Mask does not negate by itself.
Disappear disrupts the target in the Chain, while Dust removes Necrovalley, Call, Premature or Continuous cards supporting the opponent's engine.

side_plans.matchup: Book of Moon / Ring / targeted control and monster effects
side_plans.note: Tutan Mask only covers Spells/Traps that target exactly one Zombie; Wrath covers the monster-effect side that Tutan Mask cannot touch.

Virus checks the field and hand on activation, then each drawn card until the end of the opponent's third turn; it does not continuously check cards added by searches. Nobleman removes Set pieces before their FLIP effects resolve.

side_plans.matchup: Gravekeeper / Harpie / Amazoness / Field Spell backrow
side_plans.note: Dust clears Necrovalley or the opposing Field Spell; Tutan Mask then protects a key Zombie from subsequent targeted interaction.
